newsitem.title: GERMANY: Peru must use any chance to talk to hostages - Bonn.
newsitem.headline: Peru must use any chance to talk to hostages - Bonn.

text.p: Germany on Thursday urged Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori not to reject any chance to speak to the leftist guerrillas holding hundreds of hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
"I appeal to you not to rule out any possibility for discussion which would lead to a peaceful conclusion," Kinkel said in a telegram to Fujimori.
Germany's foreign ministry said on Thursday the hostages had neither enough space to sleep nor enough food.

Spokesman Martin Erdmann told journalists that the more than 400 captive diplomats, businessmen and government officials were in a precarious situation at the hands of terrorists determined to reach their goals.
But Kinkel told Fujimori he was relieved that Peru had said the safety of the hostages was its priority and that it did not plan any move which might put their lives at risk.
He repeated an offer to send a team of German police specialists to help in the crisis, and urged Lima to keep Germany's representatives fully informed about its actions.

German ambassador Heribert Woeckel, one of the diplomats released on Wednesday to help negotiations between the Lima government and the leftwing guerrillas, informed Bonn by telephone of the situation inside the residence.

"After more than 30 hours of captivity, in a psychologically difficult situation, there is not enough room to sleep, the sanitary situation is inadequate and of course the provisions are insufficient for so many people in such a crowded area," Erdmann said.
He called the situation "precarious" because, as Woeckel reported, "the hostage takers made a very calm and reasonable impression, but they also knew exactly what they want.

"They made a very determined impression. They're completely clear about their goals and want to reach these goals, that is, the release of their comrades from Peruvian, Colombian and Bolivian prisons."
"So the situation is serious. This is not a crime story that will certainly have a happy ending."
